blockAssessments.assessment: Finite equal-area aligned plates are approximated by infinite sheets only when lateral dimensions greatly exceed their separation and fringing is negligible. Equal opposite free charges and a fully filled homogeneous linear isotropic dielectric are stated. Sheet-field superposition gives the interplate E magnitude; sigma is a signed free-charge density, while magnitudes correctly appear in E.

The field direction and plate separation specify the absolute potential difference. Nonzero charge cancellation is explicit; zero-charge capacitance is its linear limiting coefficient, not0/0. Geometry, medium and external connections are fixed. SI epsilon0*epsilon*S/d has farad units; the CGSE length-unit formula is kept separate and no dimensional epsilon0=1 substitution is claimed.

The charged rod is removed before changing separation, the insulated plate approximately retains its free charge, and charging/leakage/connections/nearby bodies are controlled. With fixed area and medium, increasing separation reduces C and increases |U|. The electrometer observation is explicitly qualitative and does not determine the numerical coefficient or bypass stray-field/connection effects.
The original apparatus figure/caption slots remain exact source-bound placeholders. This textual review approves no figure pixels, apparatus inventory, geometry or rendering.

The insertion experiment keeps approximately fixed free charge after charging ceases. Ordinary insulating dielectric insertion lowers the voltage and increases capacitance. The text distinguishes a partial inserted slab from the fully filled homogeneous medium needed for the displayed simple formula; no exact relative-permittivity multiplier is assigned to an unspecified slab.

Large capacitance permits larger equal/opposite electrode charges at a given voltage, not a large net charge on the capacitor. The Earth comparison is an ideal isolated-sphere estimate. It is explicitly stated that increasing voltage at fixed C also increases plate charge. Dielectric breakdown invalidates the linear insulating model and may damage the device; arbitrarily shrinking the gap or raising voltage is not justified.

independentDerivations: Two ideal sheet contributions |sigma|/(2*epsilon0*epsilon) add between the plates. With |sigma|=|q|/S, E=|q|/(epsilon0*epsilon*S), |U|=E*d, and C=epsilon0*epsilon*S/d for nonzero charge.
Dimensions are(F/m)*m^2/m=F in SI. The electrostatic CGSE convention gives epsilon*S/(4*pi*d), a length-unit capacitance; unit conventions are not interchangeable.

At fixed free charge, increasing d lowers C and raises |U|. Fully inserting a linear homogeneous dielectric increases C and lowers |U|; partial filling cannot be assigned the same simple coefficient without its geometry.

At fixed voltage, greater C means greater electrode charge. At fixed C, greater voltage also means greater electrode charge. Equal opposite electrodes give zero net capacitor charge; dielectric breakdown is outside the assumed insulating regime.
